title: Constant module inverse image from a constant underlying set inverse image
statement: Let f:X -> U be a morphism of schemes, with X nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], and let R be a commutative ring in Type (u+1). Let F be a sheaf of R-modules on the small etale site of U [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. If the set inverse image f^{-1} of the underlying sheaf of sets of F is constant on X [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], then the module inverse image f^*F [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is constant as an R-module sheaf. No finiteness assumption is made.

proof.text: The private proved helper set_constant_sections_bijective embeds an arbitrary set E in FreeAbelianGroup E. Left exact sheafification preserves this monomorphism. Compose the embedding with the canonical sheafification/forget comparison. By lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected, the image of a global set section is the constant abelian section of some a. Choose a point of X and a local representative e of the set section on an etale neighbourhood of that point. Naturality identifies the restriction of a with the constant section of FreeAbelianGroup.of e. The neighbourhood is nonempty, so injectivity of the constant-presheaf sheafification map there gives a = FreeAbelianGroup.of e. Monicity now gives that the original global section is e. Injectivity follows from the abelian constant-section injection and FreeAbelianGroup.of_injective. This includes E empty and arbitrarily large E in Type (u+1).

The preceding bijectivity says the unit of the constant-set-sheaf/global-sections adjunction is an isomorphism at every set. Adjunction.fullyFaithfulLOfIsIsoUnit gives full faithfulness of the constant-set-sheaf functor. The set inverse image preserves finite limits: unfold it as sheafToPresheaf, left Kan extension, and sheafification; the base-change functor is flat and AB5OfSize for types supplies finite-limit preservation of its filtered left Kan extension. Apply lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-abelian-lift-hom to this finite-limit preservation. Compose its component with the underlying-set image of lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-pullback-forget-naturality to identify the underlying set sheaf of the module inverse image with the given constant set inverse image.

For G equal to the module inverse image, Mathlib constantSheafAdj_counit_w factors the forgotten module counit as the constant/forget comparison followed by the set counit. The comparison is an isomorphism since forgetting modules preserves sheafification. The set counit is an isomorphism by full faithfulness and constancy from step 2. Thus the forgotten module counit is invertible. The module-sheaf forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms, so the module counit is invertible. Its inverse explicitly identifies G with the constant module sheaf on its global sections, proving IsConstant without requiring full faithfulness of the module constant functor.
